findings.current: Murim was a world that lived up to the phrase *a mountain of swords and a forest of blades*.
findings.defect: The components of the source expression are reversed: 刀 is blade and 劍 is sword.
findings.rationale: The replacement preserves the explicit order and imagery of 刀山劍林.
findings.replacement: Murim was a world that lived up to the phrase *a mountain of blades and a forest of swords*.
findings.source: 무림은 도산검림(刀山劍林)이라는 말이 어울리는 세계였다.

findings.current: Both arms, severed below the elbows, had been treated with high-ranking healing magic and advanced potions.
findings.defect: The draft makes the healing magic high-ranking, whereas the source identifies the healer as high-ranking.
findings.rationale: 고위 modifies 힐러, preserving the person responsible for the treatment and the established term “healer.”
findings.replacement: Both arms, severed below the elbows, had been treated with recovery magic from a high-ranking healer and advanced potions.
findings.source: 팔꿈치 아래로 절단된 양팔은 고위 힐러의 회복 마법과 상급 포션으로 치료를 끝냈다.

findings.current: Potions weren’t magic wands that could fix everything.
findings.defect: The draft adds a magic-wand metaphor absent from the source.
findings.rationale: 만능이 아니다 means that potions are not universally effective, without introducing additional imagery.

findings.defect: The singular question about the bastard responsible is changed into a plural question about the attackers.
findings.rationale: 어떤 새끼 is singular, and the following narration asks who sent the Black Hunters rather than merely identifying the three assailants.

findings.current: Until then, I had no intention of sitting around with my head in the clouds.
findings.defect: “With my head in the clouds” means being dreamy or inattentive, not waiting idly without taking action.
findings.rationale: 넋 놓고 기다리다 means to wait passively or vacantly.
findings.replacement: Until then, I had no intention of sitting around and waiting.
findings.source: 그때까지 넋 놓고 기다릴 생각은 없다.

findings.current: As I had expected, Butler Kim should have been there too, but he was nowhere to be seen.
findings.defect: The opening clause incorrectly makes Butler Kim’s absence part of what the narrator expected and produces a contradictory construction.
findings.rationale: The narrator expected Butler Kim’s presence and is surprised by his absence.
findings.replacement: Butler Kim, whom I had naturally expected to be there, was nowhere to be seen.
findings.source: 당연히 있을 거라고 짐작했던 김 집사는 보이지 않았다.

findings.current: Team Leader Choi took a sip of coffee that had gone cold, its temperature matching the chilly smile at the corner of his mouth.
findings.defect: The draft transfers the cold smile from the narrator to Team Leader Choi.
findings.rationale: 내 입가 unambiguously identifies Jin Taekyung as the person smiling.
findings.replacement: Team Leader Choi took a sip of coffee that had gone as cold as the smile on my lips.
findings.source: 내 입가에 맺힌 웃음만큼이나 차갑게 식은 커피를 한 모금 마신 최 팀장이 말했다.

findings.current: > **(Best comment)** I knew this was coming. I heard about it secondhand and thought, *No way,* but I figured it would blow up someday.
findings.defect: Rendering 다리 건너 듣고 only as “heard about it secondhand” removes the bridge wording that directly sets up Taekyung’s following “What bridge?” joke.
findings.rationale: The literal bridge image must remain visible for the ensuing literal-minded threat to work; the footnote supplies the idiomatic meaning without spoiling the joke.
findings.replacement:
> **(Best comment)** I knew this was coming. I heard it across the bridge[^1] and thought, *No way,* but I had a feeling it would blow up someday.
>
> [^1]: A Korean expression meaning the information was heard indirectly.
findings.source: (Best댓글) 내 이럴 줄 알았다. 다리 건너 듣고 설마 했는데, 언젠가 한 번 터질 것 같았음.

findings.current: “This is organized. It’s clear now that they sent the Black Hunters after you from the beginning.”
findings.defect: The draft says the Black Hunters were sent after Taekyung, changing the stated target even though they attacked Im Kkeokjeong.
findings.rationale: 처음부터 노리고 describes the attack as a planned component of the broader operation; it does not say the Black Hunters were sent to attack Taekyung.
findings.replacement: “This is organized. It’s clear now that sending the Black Hunters was part of the plan from the beginning.”
findings.source: “조직적입니다. 처음부터 노리고 블랙 헌터를 보낸 게 확실해졌어요.”

findings.current: “That’s how people are. Once someone starts muddying the waters properly, it’s difficult to keep one’s balance.”
findings.defect: “Muddying the waters properly” and “keep one’s balance” form an awkward mixed metaphor that obscures the point about manipulating public opinion.
findings.rationale: The replacement naturally conveys 물타기 as deliberate narrative or opinion manipulation while preserving 중심을 잡다 as maintaining one’s judgment.
findings.replacement: “That’s how people are. Once someone really starts muddying the waters, it’s hard for people to keep their bearings.”
findings.source: “사람이란 생물이 그렇습니다. 한번 제대로 물타기를 시작하면 중심을 잡기가 쉽지 않죠.”

findings.current: “There seems to be outside pressure. The CCTV footage is in their hands as well.”
findings.defect: The pronoun “their” can refer to the investigation team from the preceding exchange, while 저쪽 explicitly points to the opposing side.
findings.rationale: The source distinguishes the investigation team from the people exerting pressure and controlling the footage.
findings.replacement: “There seems to be outside pressure. The CCTV footage is in the other side’s hands, too.”
findings.source: “역시 외압이 있는 것 같습니다. CCTV 자료도 저쪽 손에 있고요.”

findings.current: “All three have stopped answering their phones.”
findings.defect: The draft narrows a complete loss of contact into the witnesses merely declining phone calls, implying a voluntary action not stated in the source.
findings.rationale: 연락이 끊기다 means that contact has been lost, without specifying whether the witnesses are deliberately refusing calls.

findings.defect: The draft weakens the narrator’s blunt sarcasm into a vague observation.
findings.rationale: 끝내주네 is sarcastic praise here, reacting bitterly to all three witnesses becoming unreachable.

findings.current: “They seem intent on isolating us completely. The interview with Mr. Kim Sangshik is part of that.”
findings.defect: The draft changes the implied object of the isolation campaign from Taekyung to the entire group.
findings.rationale: Kim Sangshik’s interview is specifically designed to destroy Taekyung’s reputation and isolate him; Team Leader Choi is addressing Taekyung directly.
findings.replacement: “They seem intent on isolating you completely. The interview with Mr. Kim Sangshik is part of that.”
findings.source: “철저하게 고립시키겠다는 의도 같습니다. 김상식 씨 인터뷰 영상도 그렇고요.”

findings.defect: The draft omits the concrete example that explains how the media campaign will manufacture credibility.
findings.rationale: The source explicitly identifies testimony from Taekyung’s acquaintances as the mechanism, leading directly into his expectation that former coworkers will appear.
findings.replacement: For example… testimony from people who knew me well.
findings.source: 예를 들면…… 나를 잘 아는 사람들의 증언이라던가.

findings.current:
I asked Team Leader Choi, who was looking at me with an unreadable expression,

“What?”
findings.defect: The dialogue omits that Taekyung is asking why Choi is looking at him that way.
findings.rationale: 왜 그러세요 responds to Choi’s peculiar gaze rather than simply asking him to repeat himself.
findings.replacement:
I asked Team Leader Choi, who was looking at me with an unreadable expression,

“Why are you looking at me like that?”
findings.source:
알 수 없는 눈빛으로 나를 바라보는 최 팀장을 향해 물었다.

“왜 그러세요?”

findings.current: “I got along with everyone. It was such a tiny Guild.”
findings.defect: The neutral “tiny” loses the narrator’s deliberately coarse 코딱지만 한, literally “booger-sized,” description.
findings.rationale: “Dinky little” preserves the dismissive, colloquial register without forcing the literal Korean image into English.
findings.replacement: “I got along with everyone. It was such a dinky little Guild.”

findings.current: “Looking at how the article made it into the politics and society section, it seems like they even put food in some lawmaker’s mouth. You think they couldn’t buy off a few low-rank Hunters who are struggling to make ends meet?”
findings.defect: “Put food in some lawmaker’s mouth” is an opaque literal rendering that fails to communicate the implication that the lawmaker was paid off.
findings.rationale: 입에도 풀칠 좀 해 두다 is used sarcastically here to imply that money was provided to secure the lawmaker’s participation.
findings.replacement: “Looking at how the article made it into the politics and society section, it seems like they greased some lawmaker’s palm, too. You think they couldn’t buy off a few low-rank Hunters who are struggling to make ends meet?”
findings.source: “정치·사회 면에 기사 뜬 거 보니까 웬 국회의원 입에도 풀칠 좀 해 둔 것 같은데. 먹고 살기 퍽퍽한 하급 헌터 몇 명을 못 구워삶겠어요?”

findings.current: “You’re doing a little better. You’re finally capable of thinking like a worldly adult.”
findings.defect: “Worldly” softens 때 묻은, which characterizes the new outlook as jaded or sullied, while “finally capable” adds a stronger judgment than the source.
findings.rationale: 때 묻은 contrasts Taekyung’s former innocence with the cynical thinking of an adult stained by experience.
findings.replacement: “You’ve improved a little. You can think like a jaded adult now.”
findings.source: “조금은 나아졌네요. 때 묻은 어른의 생각도 할 줄 알고.”

summary: Multiple fidelity issues alter agents, targets, and causal details; several localized choices also obscure wordplay, characterization, or natural meaning.
